france/eiffel-seine.name: Eiffel Tower and the Seine
france/eiffel-seine.description: Paris icon, with river walks, cruises and the Trocadero view.
france/eiffel-seine.details: The Eiffel Tower can be climbed or ascended by lift, and tickets are timed. The Trocadero gives the classic view, and a Seine cruise at dusk passes Notre-Dame and the Louvre. Book the tower ahead, and be wary of pickpockets near the monument.

image.title: File:Pont des Invalides and the Eiffel Tower, Paris 31 August 2019.jpg
image.author: Pierre Blaché from Paris, France

france/louvre-orsay.name: Louvre and Musee d Orsay
france/louvre-orsay.description: The world most visited art museum, and the Impressionist museum in a former station.
france/louvre-orsay.details: The Louvre holds the Mona Lisa, the Venus de Milo and vast collections, so choose a few wings. The Orsay has Monet, Renoir and Van Gogh. Book timed tickets and avoid Tuesdays (Louvre) or Mondays (Orsay) when they are closed.

image.title: File:Visitors of Musée du Louvre, April 2005 (2).jpg
image.author: Syced

france/montmartre-marais.name: Montmartre and the Marais
france/montmartre-marais.description: A hilltop village of painters with Sacre-Coeur, and the medieval quarter of boutiques and cafes.
france/montmartre-marais.details: Montmartre has steep lanes, the Sacre-Coeur basilica and the Place du Tertre. The Marais has the Place des Vosges, falafel on rue des Rosiers and fashion boutiques. Both are best on foot. Evening aperitifs are a Paris institution.

france/versailles.name: Palace of Versailles
france/versailles.description: The vast palace and gardens of Louis XIV, a half-day from Paris by train.
france/versailles.details: Versailles has the Hall of Mirrors, royal apartments and gardens with fountains. Tickets are timed, and the palace is closed on Mondays. The gardens are free on most days except fountain-show days. Allow a half or full day.

image.title: File:Main Façade, Palace of Versailles, Cour Royale.jpg
image.author: Julian Lupyan

france/normandy-dday.name: D-Day beaches and Normandy memorials
france/normandy-dday.description: Omaha Beach, the American cemetery and the museums of the 1944 landings.
france/normandy-dday.details: A guided day trip from Bayeux visits Omaha Beach, the Normandy American Cemetery, Pointe du Hoc and Arromanches. The sites are moving, so allow time. The Bayeux Tapestry in town tells the 1066 story and is worth an hour.

image.title: File:VCJCS Attends D-Day 81st Anniversary Commemorations at Normandy American Cemetery and Memorial and Utah Beach (9093110).jpg
image.author: Tech. Sgt. Tinese Treadwell

france/mont-saint-michel.name: Mont-Saint-Michel
france/mont-saint-michel.description: A tidal island abbey, rising from the bay on the Normandy-Brittany border.
france/mont-saint-michel.details: The abbey stands on a rock reached by a causeway. Tides change the scenery dramatically, so check the tide times. The village is crowded in summer, and early or late visits are calmer. A guided bay walk is possible.

image.title: File:Mont Saint-Michel, Le Mont-Saint-Michel, France (Unsplash pJGNsvYB9vw).jpg
image.author: Okamatsu Fujikawa okamatsu

france/loire-chateaux.name: Loire Valley chateaux
france/loire-chateaux.description: Renaissance castles including Chenonceau, Chambord and Amboise, in a river valley of vineyards.
france/loire-chateaux.details: Chenonceau spans the river Cher, Chambord is a huge hunting lodge, and Amboise holds the grave of Leonardo da Vinci. A rental car or a small-group tour is the easiest way. Wine tasting in Vouvray and Chinon is a perfect addition.

france/bordeaux-saint-emilion.name: Bordeaux and Saint-Emilion wine
france/bordeaux-saint-emilion.description: The elegant wine capital and a medieval village of vineyards, with tastings.
france/bordeaux-saint-emilion.details: Bordeaux has a restored riverfront, the Cite du Vin museum and a historic centre. Saint-Emilion is a UNESCO village of limestone streets with underground churches, surrounded by vines. Book chateau tastings ahead.

france/avignon-provence.name: Avignon, Pont du Gard and Provence villages
france/avignon-provence.description: The papal city, a Roman aqueduct and hilltop villages in the Luberon.
france/avignon-provence.details: Avignon has the Palais des Papes and a half-bridge over the Rhone. Pont du Gard is a Roman aqueduct, and Luberon villages such as Gordes and Roussillon have ochre cliffs and lavender in July. A car makes the villages easy.

image.title: File:Pont Saint-Bénézet from the east, Avignon, 2015.jpg
image.author: DimiTalen

france/nice-riviera.name: Nice, Eze and Monaco
france/nice-riviera.description: A seaside promenade, a cliff village and a glamorous principality on the French Riviera.
france/nice-riviera.details: Nice has the Promenade des Anglais, the old town and the cours Saleya market. Eze is a hilltop village with a perfume factory, and Monaco has the casino and palace. Trains run along the coast every few minutes. Beaches are pebbly.
